```{r setup, include=FALSE}
plot_dir <- file.path(params$output, "plots/01_read_data")
if (!dir.exists(plot_dir)) {
  dir.create(plot_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

date_prefix <- format(Sys.Date(), "%Y%m%d")

# Save a plot (ggplot / Heatmap / base R)
save_plot <- function(plot_obj, filename, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  full_path <- file.path(plot_dir, paste0(date_prefix, "_", filename))

  if (inherits(plot_obj, "ggplot")) {
    ggsave(full_path, plot = plot_obj, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi)
  } else if (inherits(plot_obj, "Heatmap") || inherits(plot_obj, "HeatmapList")) {
    # ComplexHeatmap -> PDF
    pdf(full_path, width = width, height = height)
    draw(plot_obj)
    dev.off()
  } else {
    dev.copy(png, full_path, width = width * dpi, height = height * dpi, res = dpi)
    dev.off()
  }
  message("Saved: ", full_path)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  error = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dev = "png",
  dpi = 300,
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 6
)
```

# Read in the data {#read-data}

MapMet2 analyses **bone-marrow (BM)** samples of neuroblastoma (NB) patients at
diagnosis (DE), at the two treatment timepoints T1 and T2 (coded `RE1` / `RE2`
in the metadata) and at relapse (REL), together with the normal control BM
samples also used in [MapMetSC](https://github.com/TaschnerMandlGroup/MapMetSC).
BM samples are cytospins of BM aspirates, so the analysis is purely single-cell
(no spatial analysis); primary tumors are analysed in MapMetSC.

We first read in single-cell data, previously extracted from processed multi-modal (IMC, IF) images in [MapMetIP](https://github.com/TaschnerMandlGroup/MapMetIP) or downloaded from [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/13220635/files/MapMetIP_ProcessedDataset.zip). For reading the data, we use the [imcRtools](https://github.com/BodenmillerGroup/imcRtools) package. This package uses the `read_steinbock` function to read data into a `SpatialExperiment` (SPE). The [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/SpatialExperiment.html) class [@Righelli2021] is an extension of the `SingleCellExperiment` class.
For more information, please refer to `?read_steinbock`.

## Load libraries
<details>
   <summary>Load libraries</summary>

```{r load-libraries}
library(imcRtools)
library(stringr)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(circlize)
library(paletteer)
library(dittoSeq)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(ggplot2)
library(grid)  # for unit() in the cohort overview figure
```
</details>

Shared colors and the timepoint display labels (`RE1` → `T1`, `RE2` → `T2`) are defined once in `00_MapMet_color_code.R`.

```{r color-code}
for (mapmet_cc_path in c("analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R", "00_MapMet_color_code.R", "../analysis/00_MapMet_color_code.R"))
  if (file.exists(mapmet_cc_path)) { source(mapmet_cc_path); break }

# Metadata timepoint code -> display label. Control BM samples are labelled
# "control"; codes missing from TIMEPOINT_RELABEL are kept as they are.
relabel_timepoint <- function(code, control) {
  code  <- as.character(code)
  label <- unname(ifelse(code %in% names(TIMEPOINT_RELABEL), TIMEPOINT_RELABEL[code], code))
  label[is.na(label) | label %in% c("NA", "")] <- "unknown"
  label[!is.na(control) & control == "yes"] <- "control"
  label
}
```

## Read single-cell measurement

The single-cell data folder is given by `params$input` (e.g. `.../MapMetIP_ProcessedDataset` if the processed data was downloaded from Zenodo).
In [MapMetIP](https://github.com/TaschnerMandlGroup/MapMetIP), we exported single-cell marker measurements based on non-dilated and dilated (by 1px) segmentation masks to capture membrane signals. As both are required in the downstream analysis, we read in both and combine them into one SPE object, saving each expression matrix into one `assays`slot. Measurements based on non-dilated masks will be in the `assays`slot `counts` and the measurements based on dilated masks will be stored in `counts_1px`.


```{r read-steinbock}
path <- file.path(params$input)

# Read only the bone-marrow (BM) files; primary tumors (TU) and the adrenal-gland
# (AD) reference are analysed in MapMetSC.
sample_pattern <- "_BM_"

spe_0px <- read_steinbock(path=path, image_file=NULL, panel_file = file.path(path, 'NB_Panel.csv'), intensities_folder = "intensities-0px",regionprops_folder = "regionprops", graphs_folder=NULL, pattern = sample_pattern)
spe_1px <- read_steinbock(path=path, image_file=NULL, panel_file = file.path(path, 'NB_Panel.csv'), intensities_folder = "intensities-1px",regionprops_folder = "regionprops", graphs_folder=NULL, pattern = sample_pattern)

spe <- spe_0px
assay(spe, "counts_1px") <- assay(spe_1px, "counts")

rm(spe_0px)
rm(spe_1px)
```

## Read single-cell metadata

We set the `colnames` of the object to generate unique identifiers per cell.

```{r set-colnames}
colnames(spe) <- paste0(spe$sample_id, "_", spe$ObjectNumber)
```

We then read sample- and patient-specific metadata from the file provided on Zenodo [(Supplementary_Tables/20260526_Suppl_Table1.xlsx)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13220634).

```{r read-metadata}

# Supplementary_Tables may sit inside the input dir or beside it (Zenodo layout).
.suppl_cands <- file.path(c(params$input, dirname(params$input)), "Supplementary_Tables", '20260526_Suppl_Table1.xlsx')
file_path <- .suppl_cands[file.exists(.suppl_cands)][1]
if (is.na(file_path)) stop("Supplementary table not found in:\n  ", paste(.suppl_cands, collapse = "\n  "))
sample_spec_metadata <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "sample_spec_metadata")
patient_spec_clinical <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "patient_spec_clinical")
patient_spec_genetic <- read_excel(file_path, sheet = "patient_spec_genetic")

merged_data <- sample_spec_metadata %>%
  left_join(patient_spec_clinical, by = "Patient_ID")

meta <- merged_data %>%
  left_join(patient_spec_genetic, by = "Patient_ID")
```

and assign it to the colData slot in our SPE object. All BM samples are kept: control BM and NB-patient BM at every timepoint. The metadata timepoint code is stored in `timepoint_code`; `timepoint` holds the display label (`control`, `DE`, `T1`, `T2`, `REL`).

```{r add-coldata}

spe$sample <- sub("_[^_]+$", "", spe$sample_id)
spe$fm_id <- str_match(spe$sample, "_.*_(.*)_")[,2]
spe$tissue <- str_match(spe$sample, "^.*_.*_(.*)")[,2]

# Keep bone-marrow images only (safety net on top of the read pattern)
spe <- spe[, spe$tissue == "BM"]

# Metadata row of each cell, matched on sample ID + tissue
meta_idx <- match(paste(spe$fm_id, spe$tissue), paste(meta$Sample_ID, meta$Tissue))
no_meta <- unique(spe$sample_id[is.na(meta_idx)])
if (length(no_meta)) {
  message(length(no_meta), " BM image(s) without a metadata entry are dropped: ",
          paste(no_meta, collapse = ", "))
  keep <- !is.na(meta_idx)
  spe <- spe[, keep]
  meta_idx <- meta_idx[keep]
}

spe$puncture_side <- meta$Puncture_side[meta_idx]
spe$imc_score <- meta$IMC_score[meta_idx]
spe$staining_date <- meta$Staining_date[meta_idx]
spe$stainer <- meta$Stainer[meta_idx]
spe$imc_date <- meta$IMC_date[meta_idx]
spe$control <- meta$control[meta_idx]
spe$patient_id <- meta$Patient_ID[meta_idx]
spe$timepoint_code <- as.character(meta$Timepoint[meta_idx])
spe$timepoint <- relabel_timepoint(spe$timepoint_code, spe$control)

spe$stage <- meta$INSS_stage[meta_idx]
spe$progression <- meta$efs[meta_idx]
spe$death <- meta$death[meta_idx]
spe$efs_dur <- meta$efs_dur[meta_idx]
spe$death_dur <- meta$death_dur[meta_idx]
spe$X1p_loss <- meta$X1p_loss[meta_idx]
spe$X11q_loss <- meta$X11q_loss[meta_idx]
spe$X17q_gain <- meta$X17q_gain[meta_idx]
spe$MYCN_amp <- meta$MYCN_amp[meta_idx]
spe$age_diag <- meta$age_at_diag[meta_idx]
spe$therapy <- meta$therapy[meta_idx]
spe$sex_aab <- meta$sex_aab[meta_idx]

spe$ROI <- str_match(spe$sample_id, "^.*_.*_.*_.*_(.*)")[,2]
spe$year <- str_c("20", str_extract(spe$fm_id, "^[0-9]+"))

```

The resulting BM samples per timepoint (one row per sample; a sample can have several ROIs/images):

```{r samples-per-timepoint}
sample_tab <- as.data.frame(colData(spe)) %>%
  distinct(sample, fm_id, patient_id, control, timepoint_code, timepoint)

unknown_tp <- sample_tab$sample[sample_tab$timepoint == "unknown"]
if (length(unknown_tp))
  message("BM sample(s) without a timepoint in the metadata (labelled 'unknown'): ",
          paste(unknown_tp, collapse = ", "))

tp_levels <- union(TIMEPOINT_LEVELS, sort(unique(sample_tab$timepoint)))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(timepoint = factor(sample_tab$timepoint, levels = tp_levels)),
                           responseName = "n_samples"))
```

Before saving, we check the distribution of the two DNA channels across timepoints.

```{r plot-by-timepoint}

marker <- 'DNA1_Ir191_mean'
p1 <- dittoRidgePlot(spe, var = marker, group.by = "timepoint", assay = "counts") +
    ggtitle(paste(marker,  "- per timepoint"))
marker <- 'DNA1_Ir193_mean'
p2 <- dittoRidgePlot(spe, var = marker, group.by = "timepoint", assay = "counts") +
    ggtitle(paste(marker,  "- per timepoint"))
p <- (p1 | p2)

p

save_plot(p, "DNA_markers_rawdata.png", width = 24, height = 12)

```

# Patient cohort overview {#cohort-overview}

We summarise the BM cohort in a single overview figure, one column per individual: the NB patients (left) and the normal control BM samples (right). It shows age at diagnosis as a bar plot, the availability of a BM sample at each timepoint (DE, T1, T2, REL) and of a control BM sample, and sex together with the key genetic / clinical tracks (MYCN amplification, 1p loss and progression) as colored tiles; the genetic / clinical tracks do not apply to the controls and are left blank. The table is built from the sample- and patient-level metadata (`meta`), restricted to the BM samples imaged in this dataset.

```{r cohort-table}
# BM samples with images in this dataset: NB patients and control BM
bm_samples <- unique(paste(spe$fm_id, spe$tissue))
tp_cols    <- setdiff(TIMEPOINT_LEVELS, "control")   # DE, T1, T2, REL

bm_meta <- meta %>%
  filter(paste(Sample_ID, Tissue) %in% bm_samples) %>%
  mutate(timepoint  = relabel_timepoint(Timepoint, control),
         # one column per individual (the sample ID if there is no patient ID)
         patient_id = ifelse(is.na(Patient_ID), paste0("sample_", Sample_ID),
                             as.character(Patient_ID)))

# Availability tracks: the patient timepoints, plus control BM when present
avail_cols <- c(tp_cols, if (any(bm_meta$timepoint == "control")) "control")

# Sample availability: one row per individual, one yes/no column per track
avail <- bm_meta %>%
  filter(timepoint %in% avail_cols) %>%
  distinct(patient_id, timepoint) %>%
  mutate(present = "yes") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = timepoint, values_from = present, values_fill = "no")
for (tp in setdiff(avail_cols, colnames(avail))) avail[[tp]] <- "no"

cohort <- bm_meta %>%
  group_by(patient_id) %>%
  summarise(
    group  = if (any(timepoint == "control")) "control BM" else "NB patients",
    age    = round(as.numeric(first(age_at_diag))),
    sex    = as.character(first(sex_aab)),
    mycn   = as.character(first(MYCN_amp)),
    loss1p = as.character(first(X1p_loss)),
    prog   = as.character(first(efs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  inner_join(avail, by = "patient_id")

# Order: NB patients, then controls; within a group by sample-availability
# pattern (DE, T1, T2, REL), then ID
cohort$group <- factor(cohort$group, levels = c("NB patients", "control BM"))
ord    <- do.call(order, c(list(cohort$group),
                           lapply(tp_cols, function(tp) cohort[[tp]] != "yes"),
                           list(cohort$patient_id)))
cohort <- cohort[ord, ]

# Recode MYCN / 1p loss / progression to a shared yes/no/het/NA scheme so the
# genetic / clinical tracks can share one legend.
recode_ynh <- function(x) dplyr::recode(as.character(x),
  "1" = "yes", "0" = "no", "2" = "het", "9" = "NA",
  "MNA" = "yes", "nMNA" = "no", "het" = "het", "unknown" = "NA",
  "Prog" = "yes", "NoProg" = "no", "yes" = "yes", "no" = "no",
  .default = "NA", .missing = "NA")

cohort$mycn   <- recode_ynh(cohort$mycn)
cohort$loss1p <- recode_ynh(cohort$loss1p)
cohort$prog   <- recode_ynh(cohort$prog)

# Not applicable to the controls: leave these tiles blank (NA), not "unknown"
is_ctrl <- cohort$group == "control BM"
cohort$mycn[is_ctrl] <- cohort$loss1p[is_ctrl] <- cohort$prog[is_ctrl] <- NA

# sex -> f / m
cohort$sex <- dplyr::recode(as.character(cohort$sex),
  "1" = "f", "2" = "m", "female" = "f", "male" = "m", "F" = "f", "M" = "m",
  .default = as.character(cohort$sex))

# Fix patient order and factor levels
lvl_ynh <- c("yes", "no", "het", "NA")
cohort$patient_id <- factor(cohort$patient_id, levels = cohort$patient_id)
cohort$mycn   <- factor(cohort$mycn,   levels = lvl_ynh)
cohort$loss1p <- factor(cohort$loss1p, levels = lvl_ynh)
cohort$prog   <- factor(cohort$prog,   levels = lvl_ynh)
cohort$sex    <- factor(cohort$sex,    levels = c("f", "m"))
for (tp in avail_cols) cohort[[tp]] <- factor(cohort[[tp]], levels = c("yes", "no"))

message(sum(!is_ctrl), " NB patients with at least one BM sample and ", sum(is_ctrl),
        " control BM donors; individuals with a sample per track: ",
        paste(avail_cols, vapply(avail_cols, function(tp) sum(cohort[[tp]] == "yes"), numeric(1)),
              sep = " = ", collapse = ", "))
```

The panels share the same discrete x-axis (one column per individual, NB patients and control BM as two blocks) and are stacked with `patchwork`, with identical legends collected into one.

```{r cohort-overview-figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=3.4}
# Shared x-axis expansion so panels align column-by-column.
X_EXPAND <- expansion(add = 0.5)
# NB patients | control BM as two blocks; column widths stay equal across panels
GROUP_FACET <- facet_grid(. ~ group, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x")

max_age <- max(cohort$age, na.rm = TRUE)
p_age <- ggplot(cohort, aes(x = patient_id, y = age)) +
  geom_blank(aes(y = 0)) +   # keeps every column (incl. controls without age) in the layout
  geom_col(data = function(x) x[!is.na(x$age), ], fill = "grey35", width = 0.8) +
  GROUP_FACET +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = X_EXPAND) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, max_age),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(y = "age[months]") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.title.y = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    panel.grid   = element_blank(),
    strip.text   = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(3, "mm"),
    plot.margin  = margin(2, 2, 0, 2)
  )

tile_track <- function(var, fill_vals, breaks, legend_name, y_lab) {
  ggplot(cohort, aes(x = patient_id, y = 1, fill = .data[[var]])) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
    GROUP_FACET +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = X_EXPAND) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_vals, breaks = breaks, name = legend_name,
                      na.value = "white", drop = FALSE) +
    labs(y = y_lab) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      legend.position  = "right",
      legend.direction = "vertical",
      legend.key.size  = unit(0.3, "cm"),
      legend.text      = element_text(size = 7),
      legend.title     = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y     = element_text(angle = 0, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, size = 8),
      strip.text       = element_blank(),   # group labels only on the top panel
      panel.spacing.x  = unit(3, "mm"),
      plot.margin      = margin(0, 2, 0, 2)
    )
}

# One availability track per timepoint, then control BM (shared yes/no legend)
p_avail <- lapply(avail_cols, function(tp)
  tile_track(tp, COL_AVAIL, c("yes", "no"), "BM sample", paste0("BM (", tp, ")")))

p_sex  <- tile_track("sex",    COL_SEX, c("f", "m"), "sex (AAB)",             "sex (AAB)")
p_mycn <- tile_track("mycn",   COL_YNH, lvl_ynh,     "MNA / 1p loss / prog.", "MYCN amp.")
p_1p   <- tile_track("loss1p", COL_YNH, lvl_ynh,     "MNA / 1p loss / prog.", "1p loss")
p_prog <- tile_track("prog",   COL_YNH, lvl_ynh,     "MNA / 1p loss / prog.", "progression")

# ---- Stack panels; collect legends into one column ----
p_cohort <- wrap_plots(c(list(p_age), p_avail, list(p_sex, p_mycn, p_1p, p_prog)), ncol = 1) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(2, rep(0.5, length(p_avail) + 4)), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.direction = "vertical", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.justification = "top")

p_cohort

# wider for large cohorts (~0.075 in per column)
save_plot(p_cohort, "cohort_overview.pdf", width = max(9, 2.5 + 0.075 * nrow(cohort)), height = 3.4)
```

## Save object

Finally, the generated SPE object can be saved for further downstream processing and analysis.

```{r save-objects-read-data}

saveRDS(spe, file.path(params$output, "spe_01_read_data.rds"))
```
